solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Church altar he'd rebuilt after start of century

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the opening letter
the start of a word is its opening letter, here of century
something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A church's altar has been reconstructed at the turn of a new century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges ALTAR HE'D into ATHEDRAL, which goes 'after' C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is the principal church of a diocese, so it is a specific kind of church.

clue.text: Rich and thick counterpane initially placed on sheets before end of day

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word counterpane

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of sheets of paper, 500 of them

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Bedding talk: a quilt laid on the sheets at day's close, lavishly thick.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheets here are paper, not bed linen: a REAM is a bundle of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creamy has the full, smooth richness and thickness of cream.

clue.text: Item, not very credible, supported by leader of government

indicators.note: in a down entry, being supported by means the following letter sits underneath

parts.note: a thin excuse or argument is a weak, unconvincing one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of government

explanation.surface: A political story that seems barely believable, yet the head of government backs it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are general nouns for an unspecified object or entry in a list.

clue.text: Bewitch path into building?

definitions.meaning: to cast a spell over or enchant someone (stressed on the second syllable)
a doorway or way in to a building (stressed on the first syllable)

explanation.surface: A spell cast over a walkway leading into a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to enchant; as a noun it is the way in.

clue.text: CIVIC figures?

parts.note: civic figures sound like mayors and councillors, but the capitals show the word is made of the symbols C, I, V, I, C from ancient Rome's counting system

explanation.surface: Looks like a reference to town dignitaries such as mayors.
explanation.walkthrough: CIVIC is spelt entirely with letters used for numbers in Rome: C=100, I=1, V=5.
explanation.definitionFit: The letters of CIVIC are each characters from the old Latin numbering system, hence those figures.

clue.text: Notice omitted from editorial? That's an odd look

indicators.note: omitted from says the notice's letters are taken out of the editorial word

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article
an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial with a notice missing earns a funny glance.
explanation.walkthrough: LEADER is the British newspaper term for an editorial; take out AD.
explanation.definitionFit: A leer is an unpleasant, sly or suggestive glance, so a strange sort of look.

clue.text: Penny, say, or Margaret?

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
e.g., for example, is what say means in 'apples, say'

explanation.surface: Asks whether a woman is called Penny or Margaret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny, say' looks like a name given as an example, but splits into P and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Peg is a traditional pet form of the name Margaret, like Meg or Peggy; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Suggestion taken up before autumn problem

indicators.note: in a down entry, taken up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tip is a helpful suggestion
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: An idea adopted ahead of the autumn turns into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or difficulty, so a problem waiting to happen.

clue.text: See book carried by girl around the world

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so these letters go within the girl's word

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A girl takes a book with her as she travels the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Global describes something spread across or occurring all over the world.

clue.text: Be a chauvinist, getting head bitten off

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a sexist is a male chauvinist, someone prejudiced against women

explanation.surface: Someone acts like a chauvinist and gets shouted at for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting head bitten off' removes the S from SEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being or life.

clue.text: Great conductor? Most are excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Musicians thrilled by a celebrated conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially a famous conductor.

clue.text: Male that is eating corn, say, gets a headache

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the grain sits inside the letters for that is

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
corn is an example of a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A man munching corn ends up with a sore head.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe, recurring kind of headache.

clue.text: Retraction of nitrogen? A long story

indicators.note: a retraction draws something back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: nitrogen is a gas, given here as an example

explanation.surface: Withdrawing a claim about nitrogen turns into a lengthy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally an Old Norse epic of heroes and families.

clue.text: Seem ill: upset a gremlin

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feigning sickness after annoying a mischievous gremlin.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be sick, usually to avoid work.

clue.text: Third of rocks amongst various ruins, with board giving away little

indicators.note: amongst places that single letter inside the mixed letters
various suggests differing arrangements, so the letters of ruins are mixed
third of picks the third letter of the word rocks

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging or a wooden top

explanation.surface: Among the rubble of rocks and ruins lies a board that reveals nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges RUINS to INSRU, and 'amongst' puts C inside to make INSCRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inscrutable is impossible to read, revealing very little of their thoughts.

clue.text: Love new concoction of hot gin

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of hot gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: Romance as a fresh warm gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring love means zero, a score of nil.

clue.text: Worked as senior policeman in rank

parts.note: ran, as in ran a business, means worked or operated
CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Someone who served as a high-ranking officer in the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like a police rank but is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank and rancid both describe food or smells that have gone off and stink.

clue.text: Believe in arrangement not requiring immediate payment

definitions.meaning: buying now and settling the bill later

explanation.surface: Trusting in a deal that lets you pay later.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to believe; as a noun, a deferred-payment facility.

clue.text: Opponent's somewhat frantic

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word frantic is used

explanation.surface: A rival is getting a little agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who opposes something, an opponent of a policy or idea.

clue.text: Seem less controlled, put in a quandary

parts.note: be is taken loosely as seem, to exist in a certain state
wilder means more unruly, less restrained

explanation.surface: Losing self-control and leaving others baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder is to confuse someone utterly, leaving them unsure what to do.

clue.text: Runs into obstruction over a play

indicators.note: into puts the runs letter inside the obstruction's word

parts.note: a dam is a barrier that obstructs water
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dash into a barrier during a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play written for performance on stage or screen.

clue.text: Some better material seen in part of school year

definitions.text: seen in part of school year

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Better resources appear during one stretch of the school year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is part of the definition, a term being a time when things are seen in school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year is divided into terms, each a period of teaching.

clue.text: That fellow's put into care after developing wild fancy

indicators.note: put into places the male pronoun inside the reworked letters
after developing means once the letters of care have been changed into a new order

parts.note: him refers to that fellow, a male person

explanation.surface: A man taken into care goes on to develop strange fantasies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That fellow's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is'; the reworked letters of care are CERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is an impossible fantasy or illusion, after the mythical composite monster.

clue.text: £1000 gets you a piano

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds will buy you a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for a thousand of a currency and also the name of a large piano.

clue.text: Understand excavation

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for understanding and also an archaeological excavation.

clue.text: Criminal misrepresented crimes by soldier?

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the insect after the mixed letters
misrepresented means shown in a false form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a soldier ant is a type of ant, so soldier can indicate the insect

explanation.surface: A villain's crimes are misreported beside an army man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges CRIMES to MISCRE; the question mark flags that soldier hints at an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer, someone who breaks the law.
